review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no new definitions or structures. It adds two results about the existing `Module.Projective` and `Module.Finite` classes applied to `M →ₗ[A] N`: `Module.Projective.linearMap` (a theorem) and `Module.Finite.linearMap_of_projective` (an instance). I searched Mathlib for existing results of this kind. I found `Module.Finite.linearMap` and `Module.Free.linearMap` in `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/FreeModule/Finite/Matrix.lean`. Those need `Ring` and `Module.Free R M` for the source module, and they work with a chosen basis. The target instead uses `Semiring` and finite projective `M`. So it is a strictly more general variant of the same fact, not a competing version of a concept. The overlap would be at most theorem-level generalisation, which this rubric excludes. I found no Mathlib version of the projectivity statement. The two results are proved separately, but they use distinct hypotheses, and the file's docstrings explain that split. Remaining uncertainty: I did not grep exhaustively for every possible Mathlib variant of the projectivity statement.
